title: Delta Snapshot Priming and Soft Reservation Orchestrator for Warm Pools
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Dedicated fleets currently suffer from spikes in cold-start latency when tenants burst beyond their active warm residency. Existing warm-pool mechanisms load full weight snapshots and do coarse KV priming which is expensive and slow to scale when many tenants need short-lived throughput. This ticket implements a lightweight orchestrator that performs: 1) delta snapshot priming — load only model shards and weight deltas required for requested precision/quantization levels and current inference graph, 2) request-driven KV cache seeding using sampled recent requests and synthetic prefixes, and 3) soft reservation tokens that temporarily hold partial capacity (worker slots + KV budget) for a tenant during rapid ramps without consuming full dedicated capacity. Goals: - Reduce 95th/99th percentile cold-start latency by 40–60% for typical tenant bursts. - Keep additional steady-state cost <10% by using delta loads and eviction-friendly caches. - Provide clear knobs for ops: reservation TTL, admission backoff, prefetch concurrency, and tenant priority tiers. Scope: - Orchestrator service + control-plane API to request soft reservations. - Worker agent changes to accept delta snapshot manifests and staged weight application (no intrusive binary changes). - KV priming pipeline that accepts a small set of request fingerprints and produces initial KV entries. - Autoscaler integration: use soft reservation tokens as short-term admission to scale GPU pools proactively. Out of scope (initial): cross-tenant weight co-location heuristics and per-model re-compilation. Rationale: Delta loading reduces IO and time-to-usable by avoiding full weight transfers for tenants that only need subset of layers (e.g., adapter-only or low-rank adapters), and soft reservations reduce oscillation in autoscaler decisions by giving transient capacity hints without immediate long-lived provisioning.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Orchestrator exposes a POST /v1/warm-reservations API that returns a reservation token with TTL and admission policy. 2) Worker agents accept a delta manifest and transition to 'staged' state within 30s for 90% of test cases (measured on our S-1 nodes). 3) End-to-end benchmark: simulated tenant burst (10x baseline qps for 30s) shows 95p latency reduced by >=40% compared to current baseline and additional cost <10% in the same window. 4) Dashboard metrics surfaced in Console: reservation_count, reservation_success_ratio, delta_load_time_p50/p95, kv_seed_hit_ratio. 5) Integration test in CI that verifies reservations expire and that autoscaler uses reservation signals to trigger scale-up without overprovisioning. 6) Ops runbook updated with steps to tune reservation_ttl, prefetch_concurrency, and eviction thresholds.
